fields.name: ImpactPosition
fields.evidence: Size 0x18 (bg3.exe+0x6E9FE0 element size 0x18). +0..+0xB is not read as a vector by the Windows reader bg3.exe+0x1959370; only the float at +4 is used there (compared with a value returned by FUN_143c68880 for the death animation). The name is taken from eoc::death::DeathComponent (Death.h: ImpactPosition, ImpactDirection, 24 bytes together) whose values the client copies; FLT_MAX in all six floats when there was no hit.

fields.name: ImpactDirection
fields.evidence: Windows client death system bg3.exe+0x1959370 gets the component through bg3.exe+0x195CDC0 (component size 0x18) and reads +0xC/+0x10/+0x14 as one vector: its dot product with the character forward vector picks the death animation (cos 45 deg test, AnimationType 8..11) and the vector rotated into character space is stored in TriggerDeathAnimationRequestOneFrameComponent +8. FLT_MAX in all three when there was no hit.

open_questions: The component is only added through the legacy ImmediateWorldCache::AddComponent (macOS) - the writer that fills it was not found on Windows, so ImpactPosition stays a name by analogy with eoc::death::DeathComponent.
The failed raw check is a false alarm: FLT_MAX (0x7F7FFFFF) is the game default for no impact.
status_reason: the raw check failed: client entity 18014402804450261: ImpactDirection: glm::vec3 part 1 is not an ordinary float
second_pass: Settled the direction vector at +0xC from the Windows reader bg3.exe+0x1959370 (via bg3.exe+0x195CDC0); the first vec3 is read only partially (+4 as a float) and its writer was not found, so it stays medium. The raw-check failures come from FLT_MAX defaults, not from a wrong layout.
